explain.say: Stand in soft snow in shoes and you sink; put on snowshoes and you float. A foundation is a snowshoe for a building: it spreads a concentrated load over enough ground for the soil to carry it. On the board, a column brings a thousand kilonewtons down to a square pad on soil that can safely take two hundred kilopascals.

explain.say: How big must the pad be? Area equals load over allowable pressure: one thousand over two hundred, five square metres. A square two point two five metres across gives five point zero six, just enough. In real design we also add the weight of the footing and the soil on top of it.

explain.say: That is a pad footing, one under each column. Under a load-bearing wall we use a strip footing, a long continuous pad. And if the pads would cover more than about half the plan, we join them into one big slab, a raft, which also copes with soft or patchy ground. Which would suit a brick house?

The strip! Now the clever part. Under the pad, the soil pushes up at about two hundred kilopascals. Each side of the pad sticks out zero point nine metres past the column, so it acts like an upside-down cantilever. Per metre width, the moment at the column face is two hundred times zero point nine squared over two: eighty one kilonewton metres.

Flip it over: the soil pushes up, so the pad bends upward.

explain.say: So the main bars go near the bottom of the pad, the face the soil's push stretches. Then we check punching shear around the column and settlement. Wonderful! Challenge: a two thousand kilonewton column on soil with an allowable pressure of two hundred and fifty kilopascals. How wide is the square pad?

faq.a: A pad footing is a square or rectangular block of reinforced concrete under a single column. It spreads the column load over enough area of soil.
A strip footing is a long continuous footing under a load-bearing wall or a row of closely spaced columns, common for houses and low-rise buildings.

faq.q: When is a raft foundation used?
faq.a: When the soil is weak or variable, when loads are heavy, or when separate footings would cover more than about half the plan area. A raft spreads the whole building's load and reduces uneven settlement.

faq.q: How do you size a pad footing?
faq.a: Divide the column load by the allowable bearing pressure to get the area, then choose the sides. One thousand kilonewtons on 200 kilopascals needs 5 square metres, about 2.25 metres square.

faq.q: Why does a pad footing have bottom reinforcement?
faq.a: The soil pushes up on the parts of the pad sticking out beyond the column, bending them upward like upside-down cantilevers. That stretches the bottom face, so the main bars go there.
asks: Where is the steel in a footing?

facts: A raft is often chosen when separate footings would cover more than about half of a building's plan area.
In cold climates, footings are placed below the frost depth so freezing soil cannot heave them.
